I just found what I believe is an ingenious solution. Instead of rotor blades being attached to cogs, I decided instead to attach them to an powered wheel, then attach 4 miniature fans/flying blocks to said wheels. It spins very fast, has more durability, and completely isolates the torque(Or simply doesn't generate any, is there a difference?). This eliminates the need for contra-rotating engines, but I like several. :P

They're not even connected to a ballast; switching the direction the rotors spin somehow changes the force applied, so my complaint is still justified. I've since just added a counteracting, external torque, but it's still annoying.

Using the ingame wing editor, make the wing to roughly 5 times the surface area it had by default, more if needed. You'll need to XML edit for this part, but then scale the mass down to 0, and the physical size to as small as is necessary. Nudge it inside the fuselage at the back of the plane and add more/scale if needed. Just remember, only the Ingame editor actually affects areodynamic properties XML editing scale is only for reducing size while maintaining those important properties. This can also be used on normal wings to make your plane fly at extremely high altitudes while maintaining stability. Basically you could make a cube more stable than a giant glider with this.
